findings.text: follow-on: the report's fourth follow-on states the worker git shim 'multiplies git cost ~40x (202 s vs 82 s for identical input, 323 subprocess calls)'. The two walls it cites give a x2.5 wall ratio; the ~40x is a per-call factor derived from the shim's design but not shown from the profile, so the premise of the follow-on rests on an unshown quotient. A per-call figure needs the added cost divided by the 323 calls, or one git call timed with and without the shim.

follow-on: the raw attribution backing this report - prof-unfenced.prof, summary-unfenced.json, setup.py and gate-complete-profile.log - lives only under node-local $TMPDIR/complete-profile/, gone when the allocation ends. The report is durable and its numbers reconcile today, but a later reader cannot re-derive or audit the profile; the node's write scope granted the report path alone, so this is a node-design gap - grant the scratch-copy path, or have the node place summary-unfenced.json under the report's directory.

The reviewed worktree is clean at 0c81d08b with HEAD equal to the orientation base sha. The report is present at the declared path and byte-identical to the delivery copy in the run directory (diff empty). No product source, no plan HTML, no figure written. The run-dir delivery copy is written outside the literal declared path but inside the node's own run directory, where its manifest lives by contract, so it is not a foreign-path write.

justifications.durability: This is a read-only investigation, so there is no guard to revert and no regression to catch - the durability question for such a node is whether the deliverable survives and the measurement can be re-checked, and here it partly cannot. The report is durable and correct, written to the fence path with an identical copy in the run directory. But the material that backs it - the .prof, summary-unfenced.json, setup.py and the gate log - lives only under node-local $TMPDIR/complete-profile/, which dies with the allocation; the node's write scope granted the report path alone, so the worker was fenced out of placing them beside it. A later reader of the plan can read the report's table but can neither re-run the attribution nor audit the raw profile. The gap is carried as a follow-on on the node design, not a defect in the worker's work, which stayed within its grant.
justifications.evidence: Every headline number in the report reconciles with the artifacts this review opened. summary-unfenced.json records wall_seconds 81.858 and tree_state_calls 134; cum_scan_total 1.313 against cum_tree_state 1.298 with share_scan_of_wall 0.0160 (1.6%); the top-cumulative table gives functions_in 951 calls/36.31 s, promotion_clone_matches 40.24 s, read_state 205 calls/29.04 s and subprocess_run 323 calls/3.46 s - all matching the report's table. The gate log names revision 0c81d08b, the tree, the command, cwd and module.__file__. All ten cited file:line sites resolve to the exact named symbol. Reproduced independently of the report: _boundary_snapshot_roots (dispatch.py:8175) returns two roots when fenced and None otherwise, and the promotion boundary reads record['fenced'] is True to choose roots; across the 33 live pointers 30 carry fenced:true and the 3 legacy imas-efit pointers carry none, and their repository_tree_snapshot trees are exactly 207 and 214 as the report states. Held below full for two reasons: the raw profile lives only under node-local $TMPDIR, so a later reader cannot re-derive the numbers; and the '~40x git-shim multiplier' headline is not reconstructible from the two walls it cites (82 s -> 202 s is x2.5 wall). A read-only node with no guard to falsify has no negative control, which the node discloses.
justifications.fit: The report sits where the brief put it (the crew report store, copied to the run directory), is titled by what it measures, and every name and file:line it cites is real. Its follow-ons name concrete functions to bound (clones.py:278/117, metadata_index.py:411 -> _plan_html.py:482, promotion.py:5971 -> runs.py:1069, and the shim's per-call cost), which is the actionable half the plan section wants. The report is prose markdown, but the brief itself named complete-profile.md at a path outside docs/, so the HTML-for-structured-docs rule does not bind this artifact. One point withheld for the unsupported ~40x shim multiplier, which weakens one of the four follow-ons.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The brief asked to attribute one crew complete's wall time to the calls that spend it, name the top cumulative sites with call counts and the worktree count, and propose a bounding change. The node did exactly that, and it falsified the brief's named suspect: the per-worktree boundary/audit-scan figure is 1.6% of wall (1.31 s / 134 calls / 131 trees), not the dominant cost. It attributed the bulk of wall to three repository-wide analyses that do not scale with the worktree count, and separated the two regimes correctly (fenced runs bounded to two trees by code-read; legacy unfenced runs re-scan every recorded tree). Every hot path is named with file:line and four concrete follow-ons are proposed. One point withheld: the profile was taken in a scratch tree with the worker git shim off PATH, so the reported absolute seconds are not the production command's exact wall - the shimmed figure (202.09 s) is the production-shaped one and is reported beside it; a deliberate and disclosed choice, not an error.
justifications.scope_discipline: The reviewed worktree is clean at 0c81d08b with no source change and HEAD equal to the node's orientation base sha; the node left nothing in the repository. Its declared write path (the report) is present and identical to the delivery copy. Nothing foreign was touched; the run-dir copy is the node's own directory. No plan HTML and no project index was mutated.
